messages.author: c4ad98ee09d9ee51
messages.subject: scale_shape question
parts:
Hi,

I know to show points as outlines I do scale_shape(solid = FALSE) and
that will change all the points. Say that I'm plotting two data sets
and I want one to be solid and one to be an outline, is there a way to
do that?


library("ggplot2")
library("reshape")

DF <- read.table("MMOEC.csv", header=TRUE, sep=",")
new.data<-melt(DF,id.var="X",na.rm=FALSE,
measure.vars=c("Emission","MMO.645"))

G <- ggplot(new.data,aes(x=X,y=value,shape=variable))+
geom_point(size = 3, alpha = 1/2) +
#scale_shape(solid = FALSE) +
scale_x_continuous("JD - 2450000") +
scale_y_continuous("Intensity") +
coord_cartesian()


dput(head(new.data[sample(1:nrow(new.data)), ]))

structure(list(X = c(5242L, 5307L, 5300L, 5289L, 5184L, 5312L
), variable = structure(c(2L, 1L, 2L, 1L, 2L, 2L), .Label =
c("Emission",
"MMO.645"), class = "factor"), value = c(NA, 0.974457405,
2.381950804,
1.029274566, NA, NA)), .Names = c("X", "variable", "value"), row.names
= c(82L,
58L, 116L, 45L, 64L, 122L), class = "data.frame")

Thanks!

G + scale_shape_manual(values=c(19, 20))

There might be more... and there's probably a better way.
